title: Aceh War begins
summary: On 26 March 1873 a Dutch warship opened fire on the coast of Aceh, and Dutch East Indies troops were sent to take the sultan's palace in Kutaraja. A museum exhibition describes the Dutch invasion as the start of a forty-year conflict marked by strong Acehnese resistance. In a 1904 massacre at Kutö Réh, Dutch colonial troops killed 313 men, 189 women and 59 children.

uncertainty.note: Start is the first Dutch bombardment (26 March 1873) per Seasia; the war itself is described by the exhibition as lasting forty years, so the record is anchored on the start only.

importance.justification: A decades-long Dutch colonial war that ended the Aceh sultanate and killed many civilians.

audience_note: Concerns a colonial war including massacres of civilians; stated in general terms.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the war's end: the exhibition says a forty-year conflict, other sources give 1904 or later, so no end year is claimed. The Kutö Réh figures are stated by the exhibition; a Dutch-side source should confirm. The Seasia piece did not mention Banda Aceh by name; the pin follows the exhibition naming Banda Aceh as an early target.
